'''David H. Grinspoon''' (born December 21, 1959) is an American [[Astrobiology|astrobiologist]]. He is the former Senior Scientist for Astrobiology Strategy at [[NASA]]<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://astrobiology.nasa.gov/news/a-nasa-astrobiology-community-update-from-the-directors-of-the-divisions-of-astrophysics-and-planetary-science/|title=A NASA Astrobiology Community Update from the Directors of the Divisions of Astrophysics and Planetary Science}}</ref> (2023-2025) and was the inaugural [[Baruch Samuel Blumberg|Baruch S. Blumberg]] [[NASA]]/[[Library of Congress]] Chair in Astrobiology for 2012–2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.loc.gov/today/pr/2012/12-080.html|title=David Grinspoon Named to Astrobiology Chair|website=Library of Congress|language=en|access-date=2016-05-05}}</ref><ref name="Chair of Astrobiology">{{cite web|url=https://www.loc.gov/today/pr/2012/12-080.html|title=David Grinspoon Named the First Chair in Astrobiology At John W. Kluge Center|last=Urschel|first=Donna|publisher=|work=News from the Library of Congress|accessdate=30 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.loc.gov/today/pr/2012/12-080.html|title=David Grinspoon Named the First Chair in Astrobiology At John W. Kluge Center|publisher=|work=News from the Library of Congress|accessdate=30 January 2013}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.dmns.org/media/274080/david-grinspoon-resume.pdf|title=David Grinspoon, PhD|last=|first=|date=|website=Denver Museum of Nature & Science|publisher=|access-date=2016-05-05|archive-date=2013-01-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130123135208/http://dmns.org/media/274080/david-grinspoon-resume.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.denverpost.com/ci_20409509/denver-museum-curator-chosen-nasa-library-congress-astrobiology|title=Denver Museum curator chosen as NASA-Library of Congress astrobiology chair|website=Denver Post|date=16 April 2012 |access-date=2016-05-06}}</ref>

Currently he is Senior Scientist at the [[Planetary Science Institute]]. His research area is [[comparative planetology]], with a focus on climate evolution on Earth-like planets and implications for habitability. He has also studied, written and lectured on the human influence on Earth, as seen in cosmic perspective.

He has published four books, ''Venus Revealed'', which was a finalist for the [[Los Angeles Times Book Prize|Los Angeles Times book prize]], ''Lonely Planets: The Natural Philosophy of Alien Life'', which won the 2004 PEN literary award for nonfiction,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cafescicolorado.org/Grinspoon.htm |title=About David Grinspoon |accessdate=2008-04-06 |format=Biography |work=CafeSci}}</ref> ''Earth in Human Hands'', which was named one of NPR's [[Science Friday]] "Best Science Books of 2016" and ''Chasing New Horizons: Inside the Epic First Mission to Pluto'', co-authored with [[Alan Stern]].

==Early life and education==
Grinspoon was born in 1959. His father was [[Harvard University|Harvard]] psychiatrist and author [[Lester Grinspoon]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Space Scientists Share Childhood Memories Of Moon Landing |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/billretherford/2019/07/17/space-scientists-share-childhood-memories-of-moon-landing/ |last=Retherford |first=Bill| website=[[Forbes.com]] |date=Jul 17, 2019 |access-date=3 July 2022}}</ref> He holds degrees in philosophy of science and planetary science from [[Brown University]] and a PhD in [[Planetary Science|planetary science]] from the [[University of Arizona]].<ref name=":1" /> He is the nephew of real estate developer and philanthropist [[Harold Grinspoon]].

== Career ==
Grinspoon has served as an advisor to [[NASA]] on space exploration strategy,<ref>{{cite web|title=Solar System Exploration - People|url=http://solarsystem.nasa.gov/people/profile.cfm?Code=GrinspoonD|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100830075712/http://solarsystem.nasa.gov/people/profile.cfm?Code=GrinspoonD|url-status=dead|archive-date=30 August 2010|work=NASA - Solar System Exploration|publisher=NASA|accessdate=30 January 2013}}</ref> and as an Interdisciplinary Scientist on the [[European Space Agency]]'s [[Venus Express]] spacecraft mission to Venus.<ref>{{cite web|title=Venus Express: Searching for Life - On Earth|url=http://www.esa.int/Our_Activities/Space_Science/Venus_Express/Venus_Express_searching_for_life_on_Earth2|work=European Space Agency - Our Activities|publisher=[[ESA]]|accessdate=30 January 2013}}</ref> He was a science team member of the [[NASA Astrobiology Institute]] Titan Team,<ref>{{cite web|title=Members|url=https://astrobiology-beta.arc.nasa.gov/nai/teams/can-5/jpl-titan/members/|work=NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory - Titan|publisher=NASA|accessdate=30 January 2013|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20130217143258/https://astrobiology-beta.arc.nasa.gov/nai/teams/can-5/jpl-titan/members/|archivedate=17 February 2013}}</ref> and served as science Co-Investigator and team lead for Education and Public Outreach for the [[Radiation assessment detector|Radiation Assessment Detector]] (RAD) on the [[Mars Science Laboratory]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite web|title=SwRI Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD) Homepage|url=http://www.boulder.swri.edu/~hassler/rad/|work=SwRI Boulder|publisher=Southwest Research Institute|accessdate=30 January 2013}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://funkyscience.net/home/even-more-david/|title=Even more David|website=funkyscience.net|access-date=2016-05-06}}</ref> Currently he serves on the Science Team, and as Theme Lead for Atmospheric Composition for NASA's [[DAVINCI]] spacecraft mission which will launch to Venus in the 2031 timeframe.

Grinspoon has written for many outlets, including the [[New York Times]], [[The Atlantic]], the [[Washington Post]], [[Scientific American]] and the [[Los Angeles Times]]. For 15 years he wrote the bi-monthly "Cosmic Relief" column for [[Sky & Telescope]] magazine, where he is also a contributing editor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://funkyscience.net/articles/sky-telescopes-cosmic-relief/|title=Sky & Telescope: Cosmic Relief Articles|website=funkyscience.net|access-date=2016-05-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.skyandtelescope.com/about/meet-the-staff/|title=Meet the Staff of Sky & Telescope Magazine|website=Sky & Telescope|language=en-US|access-date=2016-05-06}}</ref> In addition, he has appeared several times as a guest, and also as guest host, of [[Neil deGrasse Tyson]]'s popular podcast and ''[[StarTalk Live|StarTalk]]''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.startalkradio.net/show/cosmic-queries-human-impact-on-earth-with-dr-funkyspoon/|title=Cosmic Queries: Human Impact on Earth with Dr. FunkySpoon|date=2014-06-22|website=StarTalk Radio Show by Neil deGrasse Tyson|language=en-US|access-date=2016-05-06}}</ref> live shows. Grinspoon has been featured on many television shows, including The Universe, How the Universe works, Wildest Weather in the Solar System, Chasing Pluto (for which he was also consulting producer), NOVA, Naked Science and The Planets.

He is adjunct professor of Science, Technology and International Affairs at [[Georgetown University]], adjunct professor of Astrophysical and Planetary Science at the [[University of Colorado]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Astrophysical and Planetary Science Directory|url=http://aps.colorado.edu/directory_full.shtml|work=Department of Astrophysical and Planetary Science|publisher=University of Colorado}}</ref> a former Fellow of the Institute for Cross-Disciplinary Engagement at [[Dartmouth College]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Institute for Cross-Disciplinary Engagement at Dartmouth|url=https://www.ice.dartmouth.edu/fellows-program}}</ref> and a former Distinguished Visiting Scholar in the College of the Environment at [[Wesleyan University]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2020-21: Habitability -- Cosmological, Planetary & Ethical Perspectives|url=https://www.wesleyan.edu/coe/thinktank/theme%202020-2021.html}}</ref>

In 2013, he was invited to give the Carl Sagan Lecture at the fall meeting of the [[American Geophysical Union]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}}

Grinspoon has lectured on the future of human civilization for the [[World Economic Forum]], [[United Nations]] offices in several countries and at [[Vatican City|the Vatican]].

== Awards ==
Grinspoon has won many awards including the 2006 [[Carl Sagan Medal]] by the [[Division for Planetary Sciences]] of the [[American Astronomical Society]] for excellence in public communication of planetary science; Alpha Geek 2007 by [[Wired (magazine)|WIRED Magazine]]; the 2004 [[PEN Center USA]] Literary Award for Research Nonfiction for ''Lonely Planets''; 1997 [[Los Angeles Times Book Prize]] Finalist for ''Venus Revealed''; and the 1989 [[Gerard Kuiper|Gerard P. Kuiper]] Memorial Award at the [[University of Arizona]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2018 he was awarded the Eugene Shoemaker Award by the Beyond Center at Arizona State University. In 2022 he was elected as a Lifetime [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. Asteroid [[22410 Grinspoon]], a main-belt asteroid, is named after him.

== Personal life ==
Grinspoon is a musician who has played guitar and composed for many bands. Currently, he is performing with Groovadelics, the House Band of the Universe and Durty Neil. He lives in [[Washington, D.C.]], with his wife.{{Citation needed|date=May 2016}}

==Notable works==
*''Venus Revealed: A New Look Below the Clouds of Our Mysterious Twin Planet'' (1998)
*''Lonely Planets: The Natural Philosophy of Alien Life'' (2004)
*''Earth in Human Hands: Shaping Our Planet's Future'' (2016)
*''[[Chasing New Horizons]]: Inside the Epic First Mission to Pluto'' (2018)
